title: Adjusting Imports of Processed Critical Minerals and Derivative Products
summary: The action addresses import dependence for processed critical minerals and derivative products that support defense and the nation's critical-infrastructure sectors. Its focus is the vulnerable middle of the supply chain: processing and transformation, not only extraction.
key_findings: Processed minerals and derivative products are treated as security-critical inputs.
Import dependence is connected to defense and multiple critical-infrastructure sectors.
The policy focus extends beyond mine supply to processing and industrial conversion capacity.
why_it_matters: It reinforces the need to track refining and processing chokepoints rather than equating resource ownership with usable supply.
ftfn_relevance: Strengthens the critical-minerals processing and derivative-product watch lane.
Connects trade policy with industrial capacity, input costs, and supply-chain resilience.
evidence_limits: The action does not itself measure new domestic processing capacity.
Trade effects, prices, exemptions, and substitution require later implementation and market data.
